blocks.summary: Interactive knowledge platform for AI-emitted documentation, learning notes, and reviews. Single-source JSON content, runtime renderer, no build step. Standalone-file mode for offline reading; multi-page site mode with full-text search. This page uses every primitive — hover terms, click external refs, edit the live snippet, watch the chart and diagram render.
bullets: Authoring source = JSON. The single file you hand to an AI to read, modify, or extend.
Renderer = chrome.js + renderer.js running in the browser. Custom Elements provide behavior.
Tooltips, multi-domain glossary, pinch-zoom-stable chrome, Mermaid diagrams, live snippets, citation cards, charts, syntax highlight, code folding, full-text search.
Same vocabulary covers reviews, study docs, plan reviews, team briefs.

blocks.title: Tooltip behavior to test
blocks.content: Hover a term — tooltip appears after 120ms. Move the mouse toward the tooltip — it stays visible (bridge-hover). Select text inside — it works because the tooltip is a real DOM node. Click the term — pinned (accent ring). Click again or click another term — unpinned.

content.content: A single global controller manages one active tooltip. Mouseenter triggers a 120ms show delay; mouseleave triggers a 300ms hide. If the mouse enters the tooltip during the hide window, the timer cancels. Click toggles pinned state (visible accent ring). Touch devices (matchMedia '(hover: none)') get click-only behavior. Esc closes pinned. Click anywhere outside .gloss or .tooltip-popup closes pinned.

blocks.title: What's next
blocks.lead: All review items addressed. Remaining is discretionary polish and the v2.0.0 tag.

blocks.title: Ready to tag v2.0.0
blocks.content: All review showstoppers, highs, and mediums shipped. Polish items (Mermaid SRI, element-name normalization, chrome.js split) can land in v2.x point releases. The tag itself is deferred until you say so — once cut, branches relying on v2 can pin via CDN.

steps.title: Mermaid CDN integrity hash
steps.content: chrome.js loads mermaid@10 from jsDelivr without an integrity hash. For a personal tool this is acceptable supply-chain exposure; for any team or hosted deployment, pin to a specific minor and add a verified integrity attribute.

steps.title: Element-name normalization
steps.content: <page-*>, <html-doc-*>, and unprefixed (<glossary-term>, <ext-ref>) coexist. Pick one prefix project-wide when the time is right.

steps.title: chrome.js split
steps.content: Could split into tooltip + layout + search + warnings modules. Not blocking anything; just hygiene.
